name: Jira
tagline: Create an Atlassian OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app for Jira and plug it into Composio. No review needed to share it, but users see an unreviewed-app warning.

approvalWait.asStated: Approvals take 10-15 business days, but approval times vary depending on current volume and the Marketplace team's availability.

cost.asStated: Atlassian's OAuth 2.0 (3LO) docs list no fee for creating, sharing, or listing an integration.

steps.title: Create an OAuth 2.0 integration
instructions: Sign in at developer.atlassian.com, open your profile icon → Developer console.
Click Create → OAuth 2.0 integration.
Enter an app name. Users see it on the consent screen.
Pick a grant type. Account-level: one consent covers several sites. Resource-level: tokens only work on sites the user picks.
Create one app for your product. Never ask your customers to create their own 3LO apps.

fields.label: Name
fields.hint: Shown to users on the consent screen

fields.label: Grant type
fields.hint: The original 3LO behaviour. Resource-level limits tokens to the sites picked at consent

warnings.text: Atlassian says apps that make customers create individual 3LO apps break its security requirements and acceptable use policy.

steps.unconfirmed: We couldn't sign in to the console. Which grant type Composio expects isn't documented; account-level is our pick.

steps.title: Add the callback URL
instructions: In your app, select Authorization in the left menu.
Next to OAuth 2.0 (3LO), select Configure.
Paste the Callback URL below, then click Save changes.

fields.label: Callback URL
fields.hint: Must match the Redirect URI in your Composio auth config exactly

warnings.text: Composio's Jira auth config may prefill an older /api/v1/auth-apps/add URI. Set the v3 callback in both places.

problems.q: The connection fails right after the Atlassian consent screen
a: The redirect_uri Composio sends must match the Callback URL in the console.
Check both hold the same v3 callback, with no trailing slash.

steps.title: Add the Jira API and scopes
instructions: Select Permissions in the left menu.
Next to Jira API, select Add, then Configure.
Add the classic scopes below. Atlassian recommends classic over granular scopes.
Add granular scopes only for tools that need them, e.g. read:sprint:jira-software for sprint tools.
Need Jira Service Management tools? Add that API and its scopes too.
Don't look for offline_access here. Composio adds it to the authorization URL to get refresh tokens.

fields.label: Starter classic scopes
fields.hint: Add manage:jira-project or manage:jira-configuration only if your tools need them

warnings.text: Changing scopes later makes users who already consented re-consent.
Scopes never override Jira permissions. A user without Browse projects can't read a project through your app.

problems.q: A tool fails with a scope or permission error
a: The token lacks the scope that endpoint needs. Each Jira REST operation lists its OAuth scopes.
Add the scope here and in your Composio auth config, then have the user reconnect.

steps.title: Copy the Client ID and Secret
instructions: Select Settings in the left menu.
Under Authentication details, copy the Client ID and the Secret.
Store the Secret in a secret manager, never in git.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config
instructions: Open the Jira toolkit in Composio and create an auth config.
Choose OAuth2, not API Key, and turn on your own developer credentials.
Paste your Client ID and Secret, and set the Redirect URI below.
Replace the default scopes with yours. Composio's default list is long and fails if your app lacks any of them.
Save, then copy the auth config ID (ac_…) for the next step.

fields.label: Redirect URI
fields.hint: Overwrite the prefilled v1 URL if one appears

fields.label: Scopes
fields.hint: Comma separated. Every scope except offline_access must be added in the console

warnings.text: Leave out offline_access and there's no refresh token. Connections then stop when the access token expires.

steps.unconfirmed: The link exists. We couldn't check, without logging in, whether it opens auth config creation directly. If not: Auth Configs → Create Auth Config.

a: Composio asked for scopes your Atlassian app doesn't have. Its Jira guide names this error.
Trim the auth config scopes to the ones under Permissions in the console, plus offline_access.

problems.q: The link didn't open the Jira toolkit
a: Open Auth Configs in the Composio dashboard and click Create Auth Config.
Pick Jira, choose OAuth2, and turn on your own developer credentials.

steps.title: Use the auth config in your agent
instructions: Pass the auth config ID when you create a session. Your coding agent can paste this in.
Toolkits you don't list keep using Composio's managed auth.

a: The session must include authConfigs with your ac_… ID for jira.
Toolkits not listed in authConfigs fall back to managed auth.

steps.title: Connect a test account
instructions: Start a connection for a test user. Composio asks for the Jira subdomain, e.g. acme for acme.atlassian.net.
Sign in with your own Atlassian account first. A private app only works for you.
On the consent screen, pick the same site you entered as the subdomain, then Accept.
Each consent covers one site. To add another site, the user connects again.
Users already connected through managed auth must reconnect.
steps.unconfirmed: We didn't run a full connection. It needs a Composio API key and a real Atlassian sign-in.

problems.q: 403 invalid_grant: Unknown or invalid refresh token
a: Refresh tokens rotate and expire after 90 days without use. A password change also kills them.
Have the user reconnect.

problems.q: Tools fail for a site the user can open in Jira
a: The grant doesn't cover that site. Consent only covers the sites picked on the consent screen.
Reconnect and pick that site, with its subdomain in Composio.

problems.q: The consent screen still says Composio
a: The connection used the managed auth config. Pass your ac_… ID in the session.
Existing connections keep their old config. Delete and reconnect them.

steps.title: Turn on sharing
instructions: New apps are private: only you can use them. Turn on sharing before any other user connects.
Select Distribution in the left menu and switch on the toggle in the Enable sharing section.
Fill in any vendor, privacy policy and personal data questions the form asks, then save.
No review is needed. Users will see that the app has not yet been reviewed by Atlassian.

warnings.text: Sharing doesn't list your app on the Atlassian Marketplace.

steps.unconfirmed: Atlassian's docs only describe the toggle. The vendor, privacy and personal data fields come from community reports, not docs.

problems.q: Other users can't connect, but I can
a: Your app is still private. Turn on sharing under Distribution.

problems.q: Users see that the app hasn't been reviewed by Atlassian
a: That's expected for shared apps that aren't approved. It doesn't block them.
To remove it, get the integration approved through a Marketplace listing (below).

steps.title: Get the site admin to authorize your app
steps.when: When a user sees "Your site admin must authorize this app", or their org blocks user-installed apps.
instructions: Your user can't self-approve. They send the error and your app name to their Jira site admin.
The admin opens Atlassian Administration → Apps → their site under Sites → Connected apps.
They review and authorize your app, then the user retries the connection.
If the org turned on Block user apps in Connected apps settings, only admins can install apps.

warnings.text: Admins can't revoke one user's 3LO grant. Uninstalling the app from Connected apps revokes every user on that site.

problems.q: The admin can't find the app in Connected apps
a: Check the user signed in with the right Atlassian account and picked the right site.
Then check your app requests only scopes you added under Permissions.

steps.title: List and submit for approval
steps.when: Only to remove the not-reviewed warning. Sharing works without it.
instructions: Enroll as a Marketplace Partner first: agreement, due diligence and two-step verification.
On Publish a new app, select My app isn't directly installable.
Fill in App key (can't change later), version, build number and a URL with more about your integration.
Give reviewers a test instance of your product so they can run the setup.
3LO apps get an informational listing with limited Marketplace features.
steps.unconfirmed: We couldn't open the partner portal without an account, so we haven't seen the submit form itself.

steps.title: Wait for Marketplace approval
steps.when: Only if you submitted a listing.
instructions: The Marketplace team reviews submissions in the order they arrive.
Expect a few rounds of review. Keep sharing on meanwhile; users can still connect.

wait.asStated: Approvals take 10-15 business days, but approval times vary depending on current volume and the Marketplace team's availability.
